chapter_title: The Chapter of the Three Seasons
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly cosmological and structural: it defines the three times/seasons by anchoring them to major cosmic events (First Man’s descent/ascent; construction of the universe; Ambassador’s image → final Statue). The only later material is the dialogue/hagiographic container (“apostle…disciples” Q&A attributions), which can be cleanly stripped without damaging the underlying system-teaching. No NT citation formulae or institutional/pastoral grafts appear; “Jesus” functions as a Manichaean cosmic agent within the redemption sequence, not as Gospel overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: From the time when the light came forth and was crucified in the darkness, to the season when the Statue will ascend and the entire light, which was conjoined with the darkness, will be purified and cleansed. From that time on, from that time to the season of the end totals three seasons.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution and repetition marker: "Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" and the in-line speaker tag "He says:" (compilation frame language with 'apostle').
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching content is a cosmic time-span definition (Light–Darkness mixture → purification/Statue ascent), but it enters through a Mani-community dialogue frame marked by “Once again” and “apostle…disciples,” which must be stripped.

paragraphs.core_text: Three seasons: from the time when the First Man went down to the abyss, and waged the war and the struggle against the King of the realms of Darkness and his other powers. He was victorious, while his sons remain behind with them in the worlds [... ...] in the [...] until he shall catch all of them [...] he bound them all up, so that not one of them escaped his hand. He won a great victory [... ...] The First Man spent human lifetimes and generations in the land of darkness, until he prevailed [...] he fulfilled the will of the greatness that was commanded of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological-historical exposition: First Man’s descent/war/victory and long duration in the darkness—cosmos→cosmos narration without institutional application or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Then they sent the Living Spirit, the Father of Life. He brought the First Man up from the struggle, he brought him up to the land of light. This is the first period, from the descent of the First Man to his ascent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic periodization anchored to named cosmic beings (Living Spirit/Father of Life) and a clean structural definition of the first time.

paragraphs.core_text: The second season is from the time when the First Man ascended. The Living Spirit came, and the Mother of Life. They set in order the things of the universe, they set up [...] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living set in order [...] the universe, up to the moment when they go out [...] it was reckoned to the second season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological mechanics: ordering/constructing the universe by the divine hypostases; numbered-season structure continues with no editorial pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the universe [...] the Third Ambassador spread [...] that is in the [...] living; he [...] he separated beauty from all the powers and scooped it up to the heights, he swept the waste to the abyss, and he [... ...] Now, from the moment when the Ambassador revealed his image he purified the light. Sin spurted up towards him. He hid his image. Sin came [...] from the darkness. It sculpted the trees and the abortions fell down. Afterwards they sculpted Adam and Eve in the flesh. Until the moment when Jesus was sent and he [...] as he performed there his will. He gave the hope to Adam, and ascended to the heights.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-agent sequence (Third Ambassador, Image, Sin as a personified power, Adam/Eve fabrication, Jesus as redeemer agent) remains internal to Manichaean cosmology; no Gospel citation markers or church application.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, from the time when the Ambassador displayed his image until the season when the Statue will ascend at the end, shall be reckoned to the third season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise structural definition of the third season using cosmic termini (Image revelation → Statue ascent).
Pure dialogue apparatus (“disciples…apostle”) with no recoverable teaching content; functions as compilation frame.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] lasts long in the time that the First Man spent in the world of darkness. It is a very great count of time, more than the (other) two seasons!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: "The apostle says to them [...]" and omitted the manuscript page marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying teaching is comparative time-measure (duration of First Man’s period vs the other two), but presented inside Q&A frame language.

paragraphs.core_text: The first season, which the First Man spent in the world of darkness, is how much longer than the time that this universe has been? While it is established?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution: "His disciples say to him:" (Q&A frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question about comparative durations; frame attribution is late, but the queried structure belongs to the systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: If you should say that [... ...] it is small, if you should [... ...] to him [...] and you consult [...] you will tell him: Twenty times! It is greater again in this other one that you will consult: Thirty times! Less also is this other one [... ...] people will receive the of the trees [... ...] the years and the generations [...] earth to the heights. This is [...
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed reply attribution: "[He replies to them]:" (dialogue frame) and removed empty curly-brace artifact "{}" per extraction rules.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Comparative/analogical quantification of the seasons’ lengths (rhetorical second-person but not pastoral/institutional); the speaker-tag is a later dialogue wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the third period, from the time when the Ambassador revealed his image until the Statue will ascend from the lump. It again, that time, is greater than the intermediate; but it does not come equal to the time of the First Man. For this intermediate season, in which the Father of Life and the Mother of Life constructed the universe with its orders, is shorter than that of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic comparison across the three times; cosmos-only referents (Ambassador/Image, Statue, Father/Mother of Life) and impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Great is the period of the First Man! It lasts longer than the season in which the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the world and the Statue ascends. From the time too when the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the universe [... ...] when the Father of Life and the Mother of Life shaped the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core reiteration of relative durations and cosmic endpoints (dissolution, Statue ascent) with no institutional or citation intrusion.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the [...] three periods of time that occur.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Formal closure of the teaching sequence; still internal to the structural cosmology (summary of the three times).
